_general_safety: Seatbelt fastened before you move, and keep it on for the whole task.
Check mirrors and cameras, and sound the horn before you start moving.

_weather.rain: It is raining: reduce travel speed, avoid side slopes over 15 degrees, and allow extra stopping distance.
_weather.heavy_rain: Heavy rain: travel slowly, stay off side slopes, watch for soft ground and trench-edge collapse, and stop if visibility drops.
_weather.dust: Dusty conditions: keep lights on, slow down, and stop if you lose sight of ground crew.
_weather.snow: Snow and ice: travel slowly, avoid slopes, and warm up the hydraulics before full loads.

_temperature.hot: High temperature: stay hydrated and watch the coolant temperature gauge.
_temperature.cold: Below freezing: warm up the hydraulic system for five minutes before working.

safety: Confirm underground utilities are marked before the first bite.
Keep the tracks at least one metre back from the trench edge.
Nobody enters the trench or the swing radius while you are digging.

steps.do: Position the machine square to the trench line with the tracks parallel to it.
steps.why: It keeps the machine stable and the trench straight.

steps.do: Take shallow, even passes instead of one deep bite.
steps.why: It reduces wall collapse and strain on the boom.

steps.do: Place spoil at least half a metre back from the edge, on the side away from the crew.
steps.why: Spoil near the edge adds load and can slide back in.

steps.do: Check the grade with the spotter every few metres.
steps.why: Fixing depth early is much cheaper than re-digging.

trenching.tip: Keep the bucket curl smooth while crowding, and fill the bucket fully each pass.

safety: Never swing the bucket over the truck cab.
The truck driver stays in the cab, or well outside the swing radius.
Wait for the truck to stop fully, and for the driver's signal, before loading.

steps.do: Set the truck at a 30 to 45 degree swing angle.
steps.why: Every extra 15 degrees of swing adds about a second per cycle.

steps.do: Load the front of the truck bed first, then the back.
steps.why: It keeps the truck's axle loads balanced.

steps.do: Lower the bucket close to the bed before dumping.
steps.why: It prevents spillage and damage to the truck.

steps.do: Count the passes to hit the target load without overloading.
steps.why: Overloads damage haul trucks and slow the whole cycle.

truck_loading.tip: Have the next bucket full and ready while the truck positions.

safety: Confirm the trench is empty of people and equipment before backfilling.
Keep the machine off the trench edge while pushing material in.

steps.do: Place material in even layers of about 300 millimetres.
steps.why: Even layers compact properly and prevent settling later.

steps.do: Push material in from the side instead of dropping it from height.
steps.why: Dropping material can damage pipes and utilities.

steps.do: Let the compaction crew finish each layer before adding the next.
steps.why: Uncompacted layers fail inspection and must be dug out.

backfill.tip: Keep the spoil pile close so each cycle stays short.

safety: Watch for survey stakes and ground crew, and look behind before every reverse.
Keep blade loads moderate on slopes to stay stable.

steps.do: Walk or review the area first, and note high and low spots.
steps.why: Planning the passes saves time and fuel.

steps.do: Make long, overlapping passes at a steady speed.
steps.why: Consistent speed gives a smoother finish.

steps.do: Cut high spots and fill low spots in the same pass where possible.
steps.why: It avoids double handling of material.

steps.do: Check the grade against the stakes after each few passes.
steps.why: Small corrections are easier than rework.

grading.tip: Keep a full, rolling load in front of the blade.

safety: Keep ground crew away from the toe of the pile.

steps.do: Build the pile in layers instead of pushing over the top edge.
steps.why: Layered piles are stable and don't slump.
It speeds up each cycle and keeps the machine level.

steps.do: Keep material types separate as marked.

stockpiling.tip: Plan the pile shape so you never have to push uphill with a full load.
